name: license_status
description: Show whether this server runs in free or Pro mode and where to upgrade.

name: license_activate
description: Activate a Pro license key (format MCPL1.xxx.yyy). Verified offline and saved locally.

arguments.name: key
arguments.desc: License key from the checkout confirmation page

name: ics_import
description: Read a calendar export and keep it locally under a name. Give exactly one of path (a .ics file on this machine), text (the file contents pasted in), or url (a public .ics or webcal feed; Pro). Google Calendar, Apple Calendar and Outlook exports are all read. Importing the same name again replaces that calendar.

arguments.name: path
arguments.desc: Path to a .ics file on this machine

arguments.name: url
arguments.desc: Public https:// or webcal:// .ics feed. Fetched once, only because you asked; Pro feature

arguments.name: text
arguments.desc: The .ics file contents, pasted

arguments.name: name
arguments.desc: What to call this calendar, e.g. "work" or "family"

name: calendars_list
description: Every calendar imported into this server: its name, where it came from, how many event definitions it holds and when it was imported.

name: events_list
description: Every event between two dates, with recurring events expanded to their real occurrences and sorted by start. Times are shown in your own zone (the shared business profile's timezone, else this machine's) unless you pass zone. Each row carries an id you can pass to event_export or event_to_time_entry.

arguments.name: calendar
arguments.desc: One calendar name; default every imported calendar

arguments.name: from
arguments.desc: First day, YYYY-MM-DD

arguments.name: to
arguments.desc: Last day, YYYY-MM-DD, included

arguments.name: zone
arguments.desc: Show local times in this zone or city instead of your own

name: events_search
description: Find events whose title, description, location or attendees contain a phrase. Searches every imported calendar. Without from/to it looks a year back and a year forward on Pro, and the free window either side of today.

arguments.name: query
arguments.desc: Words to look for, case-insensitive

arguments.name: from
arguments.desc: First day, YYYY-MM-DD

arguments.name: to
arguments.desc: Last day, YYYY-MM-DD, included

name: free_busy
description: Where the time actually went and what is left: merged busy blocks from the calendars you name, and the gaps inside your working hours where nothing is booked. Events marked free/transparent do not count as busy; whole-day events block the day.

arguments.name: calendars
arguments.desc: Calendar names; default all of them

arguments.name: from
arguments.desc: First day, YYYY-MM-DD

arguments.name: to
arguments.desc: Last day, YYYY-MM-DD, included

arguments.name: work_start
arguments.desc: Start of your working day, HH:MM, default 09:00

arguments.name: work_end
arguments.desc: End of your working day, HH:MM, default 17:00

arguments.name: zone
arguments.desc: Zone the working hours and the output are in; default your own

name: conflicts
description: Every pair of events that overlap in time, with how many minutes they collide. Across all imported calendars unless you name one, so a work meeting clashing with a family event is caught. Whole-day events are reported separately from timed clashes.

arguments.name: calendar
arguments.desc: One calendar name; default every imported calendar

arguments.name: from
arguments.desc: First day, YYYY-MM-DD

arguments.name: to
arguments.desc: Last day, YYYY-MM-DD, included

name: next_event
description: The next event that has not started yet, with how long until it begins. Looks ahead up to a year.

arguments.name: calendar
arguments.desc: One calendar name; default every imported calendar

name: event_export
description: Write chosen events to a new .ics file you can send or import elsewhere. Either pass ids (from events_list) or a from/to window to export everything in it. Times are written in UTC so the file lands correctly in any client.

arguments.name: ids
arguments.desc: Event ids from events_list, events_search or next_event

arguments.name: from
arguments.desc: First day, YYYY-MM-DD (alternative to ids)

arguments.name: to
arguments.desc: Last day, YYYY-MM-DD, included

arguments.name: calendar
arguments.desc: With from/to: limit to one calendar

arguments.name: out_path
arguments.desc: Where to write the .ics file

name: event_to_time_entry
description: Take one event and return the exact arguments for the time-tracker's entry_add, so a meeting that already happened becomes billable time without retyping it. It does not write anything: pass the JSON straight to entry_add.

arguments.name: event_id
arguments.desc: Event id from events_list, events_search or next_event

arguments.name: project
arguments.desc: Project or client the meeting is billed to

arguments.name: rate
arguments.desc: Hourly rate for this entry; a number (120) or the words the user said ('120 euros an hour')

name: ics_forget
description: Remove one imported calendar and the local copy of its .ics file. Nothing else is touched.

arguments.name: name
arguments.desc: The calendar name from calendars_list
